sanskrit: pradiśañ śarasaṃpātān kuntīputro 'rjunas tadā sikatā vapan savyasācī rājānam anugacchati
english: Pointing out the ranges of arrow-fall, Arjuna the son of Kuntī — the ambidextrous one — walked behind the king, scattering sand as he went.

sanskrit: asaktāḥ sikatās tasya yathā saṃprati bhārata asaktaṃ śaravarṣāṇi tathā mokṣyati śatruṣu
english: "Just as this sand does not cling to him now, O Bharata, so too shall he release showers of arrows unstoppably upon his enemies."

sanskrit: na me kaś cid vijānīyān mukham adyeti bhārata mukham ālipya tenāsau sahadevo 'pi gacchati
english: "Let no one recognize my face today" — so saying, O Bharata, Sahadeva smeared his face and walked on in that manner.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ manāṃsy ādadeyaṃ mārge strīṇām iti prabho pāṃsūpacitasarvāṅgo nakulas tena gacchati
english: "Let me not attract the minds of women along the road" — so thinking, O lord, Nakula covered his entire body with dust and walked on for that reason.

sanskrit: ekavastrā tu rudatī muktakeśī rajasvalā śoṇitāktārdravasanā draupadī vākyam abravīt
english: Draupadī, clad in a single garment, weeping, her hair unbound, in her monthly season, her wet garment stained with blood, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yatkṛte 'ham imāṃ prāptā teṣāṃ varṣe caturdaśe hatapatyo hatasutā hatabandhujanapriyāḥ
english: "For whose sake I have come to this state — in the fourteenth year from now, their wives shall be widowed, their sons slain, their dear kinsmen destroyed."

sanskrit: bandhuśoṇitadigdhāṅgyo muktakeśyo rajasvalāḥ evaṃ kṛtodakā nāryaḥ pravekṣyanti gajāhvayam
english: "Smeared with the blood of their kinsmen, their hair unbound, in their seasons, having performed such water-rites — thus shall the women enter Hāstinapura."

sanskrit: kṛtvā tu nairṛtān darbhān dhīro dhaumyaḥ purohitaḥ sāmāni gāyan yāmyāni purato yāti bhārata
english: The steadfast priest Dhaumya, having strewn the kusha-grass in the direction of the southwest, walked ahead singing the Sama hymns addressed to Yama, O Bharata.

sanskrit: hateṣu bhārateṣv ājau kurūṇāṃ guravas tadā evaṃ sāmāni gāsyantīty uktvā dhaumyo 'pi gacchati
english: "When the Bharatas are slain in battle, the preceptors of the Kurus shall sing such Sama hymns then" — saying this, Dhaumya too walked on.

sanskrit: hā hā gacchanti no nāthāḥ samavekṣadhvam īdṛśam iti paurāḥ suduḥkhārtāḥ krośanti sma samantataḥ
english: "Alas, alas, our protectors are leaving — behold this sight!" — thus the citizens, stricken with great grief, cried out on all sides.

sanskrit: evam ākāraliṅgais te vyavasāyaṃ manogatam kathayantaḥ sma kaunteyā vanaṃ jagmur manasvinaḥ
english: Through such outward signs and gestures, conveying the resolve that lay within their minds, the noble sons of Kuntī departed to the forest.

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣu narāgryeṣu niryatsu gajasāhvayāt anabhre vidyutaś cāsan bhūmiś ca samakampata
english: As these foremost of men departed from Hāstinapura, lightning flashed in a cloudless sky and the earth trembled.

sanskrit: rāhur agrasad ādityam aparvaṇi viśāṃ pate ulkā cāpy apasavyaṃ tu puraṃ kṛtvā vyaśīryata
english: Rāhu swallowed the sun outside of an eclipse, O lord of the people; and a meteor fell, circling the city counter-clockwise before crashing down.

sanskrit: pravyāharanti kravyādā gṛdhragomāyuvāyasāḥ devāyatanacaityeṣu prākārāṭṭālakeṣu ca
english: Flesh-eating creatures — vultures, jackals, and crows — cried out ominously at the temples, shrines, and on the ramparts and turrets.

sanskrit: evam ete mahotpātā vanaṃ gacchati pāṇḍave bhāratānām abhāvāya rājan durmantrite tava
english: Such were these great evil omens as the Pāṇḍava went to the forest — portending, O king, the destruction of the Bharatas through your ill counsel.

sanskrit: nāradaś ca sabhāmadhye kurūṇām agrataḥ sthitaḥ maharṣibhiḥ parivṛto raudraṃ vākyam uvāca ha
english: Nārada, standing in the midst of the assembly hall before the Kurus, surrounded by great sages, spoke these dreadful words.

sanskrit: itaś caturdaśe varṣe vinaṅkṣyantīha kauravāḥ duryodhanāparādhena bhīmārjunabalena ca
english: "Fourteen years from now, the Kauravas shall be destroyed here — through the transgression of Duryodhana and by the might of Bhīma and Arjuna."

sanskrit: ity uktvā divam ākramya kṣipram antaradhīyata brāhmīṃ śriyaṃ suvipulāṃ bibhrad devarṣisattamaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the greatest of divine sages, bearing the vast brahminical splendour, ascended to heaven and swiftly vanished.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ karṇaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ droṇaṃ dvīpam amanyanta rājyaṃ cāsmai nyavedayan
english: Then Duryodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala regarded Droṇa as their island of refuge and surrendered the kingdom to him.

sanskrit: athābravīt tato droṇo duryodhanam amarṣaṇam duḥśāsanaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca sarvān eva ca bhāratān
english: Then Droṇa spoke to the wrathful Duryodhana, to Duḥśāsana, to Karṇa, and to all the Bharatas.

sanskrit: avadhyān pāṇḍavān āhur devaputrān dvijātayaḥ ahaṃ tu śaraṇaṃ prāptān vartamāno yathābalam
english: "The twice-born declare the Pāṇḍavas, sons of gods, to be inviolable. I, for my part, while I live, protect those who have sought my shelter to the best of my power.

sanskrit: gatān sarvātmanā bhaktyā dhārtarāṣṭrān sarājakān notsahe samabhityaktuṃ daivamūlam ataḥ param
english: "The Dhārtarāṣṭras, together with the king, have gone over to my side with whole-souled devotion; I cannot in conscience abandon them — hence my conduct hereafter is rooted in fate.

sanskrit: dharmataḥ pāṇḍuputrā vai vanaṃ gacchanti nirjitāḥ te ca dvādaśa varṣāṇi vane vatsyanti kauravāḥ
english: "The sons of Pāṇḍu, defeated, are going to the forest in accordance with dharma; and for twelve years these Kauravas shall dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: caritabrahmacaryāś ca krodhāmarṣavaśānugāḥ vairaṃ pratyānayiṣyanti mama duḥkhāya pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Having lived the life of chastity, driven by anger and indignation, the Pāṇḍavas will bring back their enmity — to my sorrow."

sanskrit: mayā tu bhraṃśito rājyād drupadaḥ sakhivigrahe putrārtham ayajat krodhād vadhāya mama bhārata
english: "Now, I had deprived Drupada of his kingdom in a quarrel over friendship; and in his fury, for the sake of a son to kill me, he performed a sacrifice, O Bharata.

sanskrit: yājopayājatapasā putraṃ lebhe sa pāvakāt dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ draupadīṃ ca vedīmadhyāt sumadhyamām
english: "Through the austerities of Yaja and Upayāja he obtained from the sacred fire Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and from the midst of the altar the fair-waisted Draupadī.

sanskrit: jvālāvarṇo devadatto dhanuṣmān kavacī śarī martyadharmatayā tasmād iti māṃ bhayam āviśat
english: "He is flame-hued, bow-bearing, clad in armour, quiver-bearing, divine-born yet subject to mortal law — therefore fear of him entered me.

sanskrit: gato hi pakṣatāṃ teṣāṃ pārṣataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ sṛṣṭaprāṇo bhṛśataraṃ tasmād yotsye tavāribhiḥ
english: "The bull among men, the son of Pṛṣata, has indeed gone over to their side, his life-breath set free for this purpose; therefore shall I fight all the harder against your enemies."

sanskrit: madvadhāya śruto hy eṣa loke cāpy ativiśrutaḥ nūnaṃ so 'yam anuprāptas tvatkṛte kālaparyayaḥ
english: "For it is well known in the world, and proclaimed far and wide, that he was born to slay me; surely this turn of time has come upon us through your doing.

sanskrit: tvaritāḥ kuruta śreyo naitad etāvatā kṛtam muhūrtaṃ sukham evaitat tālacchāyeva haimanī
english: "Act swiftly for your well-being — this has not been accomplished by what you have done so far. This happiness is but momentary, like the shade of a palm tree in winter.

sanskrit: yajadhvaṃ ca mahāyajñair bhogān aśnīta datta ca itaś caturdaśe varṣe mahat prāpsyatha vaiśasam
english: "Perform great sacrifices, enjoy pleasures, give in charity — for fourteen years from now you shall suffer a great catastrophe.

sanskrit: duryodhana niśamyaitat pratipadya yathecchasi sāma vā pāṇḍaveyeṣu prayuṅkṣva yadi manyase
english: "Duryodhana, having heard this, act as you see fit; employ conciliation towards the Pāṇḍavas if you think it right."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca droṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd idam samyag āha guruḥ kṣattar upāvartaya pāṇḍavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Droṇa's words, Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke thus: "The preceptor speaks rightly. Vidura, bring the Pāṇḍavas back."

sanskrit: yadi vā na nivartante satkṛtā yāntu pāṇḍavāḥ saśastrarathapādātā bhogavantaś ca putrakāḥ
english: "Or if they will not return, let the Pāṇḍavas go honoured — with weapons, chariots, and infantry, provided with all enjoyments, O son."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vanaṃ gateṣu pārtheṣu nirjiteṣu durodare dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahārāja tadā cintā samāviśat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the sons of Pṛthā, defeated in that wicked game, had gone to the forest, anxiety seized Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great king.

sanskrit: taṃ cintayānam āsīnaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram niḥśvasantam anekāgram iti hovāca saṃjayaḥ
english: As Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, sat lost in thought, sighing, his mind distracted, Sañjaya spoke to him thus.

sanskrit: avāpya vasusaṃpūrṇāṃ vasudhāṃ vasudhādhipa pravrājya pāṇḍavān rājyād rājan kim anuśocasi
english: "Having obtained the earth full of wealth, O lord of the earth, and having banished the Pāṇḍavas from the kingdom, O king, why do you grieve?"

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca aśocyaṃ tu kutas teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ vairaṃ bhaviṣyati pāṇḍavair yuddhaśauṇḍair hi mitravadbhir mahārathaiḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "How should they not be grieved for, those with whom a great feud shall arise — with the Pāṇḍavas, mighty warriors eager for battle, who are like friends to great car-warriors?"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tavedaṃ sukṛtaṃ rājan mahad vairaṃ bhaviṣyati vināśaḥ sarvalokasya sānubandho bhaviṣyati
english: Sañjaya said: "This was well done by you, O king — a great enmity shall arise; the destruction of all the world along with its dependants shall come to pass."

sanskrit: vāryamāṇo 'pi bhīṣmeṇa droṇena vidureṇa ca pāṇḍavānāṃ priyāṃ bhāryāṃ draupadīṃ dharmacāriṇīm
english: "Though restrained by Bhīṣma, by Droṇa, and by Vidura — Draupadī, the beloved wife of the Pāṇḍavas, the righteous one —

sanskrit: prāhiṇod ānayeheti putro duryodhanas tava sūtaputraṃ sumandātmā nirlajjaḥ prātikāminam
english: "— your son Duryodhana, foolish and shameless, sent the charioteer's son Pratikamin, saying 'Bring her here.'"

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yasmai devāḥ prayacchanti puruṣāya parābhavam buddhiṃ tasyāpakarṣanti so 'pācīnāni paśyati
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "When the gods wish to bring ruin upon a man, they first remove his understanding; he then sees things in reverse."

sanskrit: buddhau kaluṣabhūtāyāṃ vināśe pratyupasthite anayo nayasaṃkāśo hṛdayān nāpasarpati
english: "When the intellect has become turbid and destruction stands at hand, what looks like wise counsel but is its opposite does not depart from the heart."

sanskrit: anarthāś cārtharūpeṇa arthāś cānartharūpiṇaḥ uttiṣṭhanti vināśānte naraṃ tac cāsya rocate
english: "Harmful things arise in the form of beneficial, and beneficial things in the form of harmful, when a man's end is near — and he delights in that which harms him."

sanskrit: na kālo daṇḍam udyamya śiraḥ kṛntati kasya cit kālasya balam etāvad viparītārthadarśanam
english: "Time does not cut off anyone's head by raising a stick; the power of Time is just this — the perception of things in reverse."

sanskrit: āsāditam idaṃ ghoraṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam pāñcālīm apakarṣadbhiḥ sabhāmadhye tapasvinīm
english: "This dreadful, turbulent, hair-raising act was committed by those who dragged Pāñcālī, the afflicted one, into the midst of the assembly hall —

sanskrit: ayonijāṃ rūpavatīṃ kule jātāṃ vibhāvarīm ko nu tāṃ sarvadharmajñāṃ paribhūya yaśasvinīm
english: "— she who was not born of a womb, who is beautiful, born in a noble lineage, brilliant, knowing all dharma, glorious — who could dishonour such a one?"

sanskrit: paryānayet sabhāmadhyam ṛte durdyūtadevinam strīdharmiṇīṃ varārohāṃ śoṇitena samukṣitām
english: "Who would drag into the assembly hall a woman observing a woman's duty, of lovely form, stained with blood — except one made wicked by evil gambling?"

sanskrit: ekavastrāṃ ca pāñcālīṃ pāṇḍavān abhyavekṣatīm hṛtasvān bhraṣṭacittāṃs tān hṛtadārān hṛtaśriyaḥ
english: "Pāñcālī, clad in a single garment, gazed upon the Pāṇḍavas — those whose wealth was taken, whose minds were shattered, whose wives and prosperity were seized."

sanskrit: vihīnān sarvakāmebhyo dāsabhāvavaśaṃ gatān dharmapāśaparikṣiptān aśaktān iva vikrame
english: "Stripped of all their desires, reduced to the state of slaves, bound by the fetters of dharma, rendered incapable as if of all exertion."

sanskrit: kruddhām amarṣitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ duḥkhitāṃ kurusaṃsadi duryodhanaś ca karṇaś ca kaṭukāny abhyabhāṣatām
english: "To Kṛṣṇa who was furious, indignant, and suffering in the Kuru assembly, Duryodhana and Karṇa spoke bitter words."

sanskrit: tasyāḥ kṛpaṇacakṣurbhyāṃ pradahyetāpi medinī api śeṣaṃ bhaved adya putrāṇāṃ mama saṃjaya
english: "The earth itself might burn from the glance of her pitiable eyes — that any of my sons should survive today, Sañjaya!"

sanskrit: bhāratānāṃ striyaḥ sarvā gāndhāryā saha saṃgatāḥ prākrośan bhairavaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāṃ sabhāgatām
english: "All the women of the Bharatas, gathered together with Gāndhārī, wailed terribly there upon seeing Kṛṣṇa brought into the assembly hall."

sanskrit: agnihotrāṇi sāyāhne na cāhūyanta sarvaśaḥ brāhmaṇāḥ kupitāś cāsan draupadyāḥ parikarṣaṇe
english: "The sacred fires were not invoked in the evening rite anywhere at all; the brahmins were enraged at the dragging of Draupadī."

sanskrit: āsīn niṣṭānako ghoro nirghātaś ca mahān abhūt divolkāś cāpatan ghorā rāhuś cārkam upāgrasat aparvaṇi mahāghoraṃ prajānāṃ janayan bhayam
english: "There was a terrible thunderous roar, and a great clap without cloud; dreadful meteors fell from the sky, and Rāhu swallowed the sun outside of eclipse — generating great terror among the people."

sanskrit: tathaiva rathaśālāsu prādurāsīd dhutāśanaḥ dhvajāś ca vyavaśīryanta bharatānām abhūtaye
english: "Likewise in the chariot-halls fire appeared on its own; and the battle-standards of the Bharatas shattered — portending their ruin."

sanskrit: duryodhanasyāgnihotre prākrośan bhairavaṃ śivāḥ tās tadā pratyabhāṣanta rāsabhāḥ sarvatodiśam
english: "Jackals cried out terribly at Duryodhana's sacrificial fire; and at that moment donkeys brayed in response from every direction."

sanskrit: prātiṣṭhata tato bhīṣmo droṇena saha saṃjaya kṛpaś ca somadattaś ca bāhlīkaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: "Then Bhīṣma, O Sañjaya, departed together with Droṇa; as did Kṛpa, Somadatta, and the great car-warrior Bahlika."

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ tatra vidureṇa pracoditaḥ varaṃ dadāni kṛṣṇāyai kāṅkṣitaṃ yad yad icchati
english: "Then I spoke there, urged on by Vidura: 'I grant a boon to Kṛṣṇa — whatever she desires, whatever she wishes for.'"

sanskrit: avṛṇot tatra pāñcālī pāṇḍavān amitaujasaḥ sarathān sadhanuṣkāṃś cāpy anujñāsiṣam apy aham
english: "Pāñcālī then chose the Pāṇḍavas of boundless might, with their chariots and their bows; and I too gave my assent to it."

sanskrit: athābravīn mahāprājño viduraḥ sarvadharmavit etadantāḥ stha bharatā yad vaḥ kṛṣṇā sabhāṃ gatā
english: "Then the greatly wise Vidura, knower of all dharma, spoke: 'O Bharatas, you have reached the end of yourselves by the fact that Kṛṣṇa was brought into the assembly.'"

sanskrit: eṣā pāñcālarājasya sutaiṣā śrīr anuttamā pāñcālī pāṇḍavān etān daivasṛṣṭopasarpati
english: "'This daughter of the Pāñcāla king — this peerless goddess of fortune — Pāñcālī approaches these Pāṇḍavas as one sent by fate.'"

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pārthāḥ parikleśaṃ na kṣaṃsyante 'tyamarṣaṇāḥ vṛṣṇayo vā maheṣvāsāḥ pāñcālā vā mahaujasaḥ
english: "'The sons of Pṛthā, being highly intolerant, will not forgive the wrong done to her — nor will the mighty-armed Vṛṣṇis, nor the greatly powerful Pāñcālas.'"

sanskrit: tena satyābhisaṃdhena vāsudevena rakṣitāḥ āgamiṣyati bībhatsuḥ pāñcālair abhirakṣitaḥ
english: "'Protected by Vāsudeva, that one true to his pledges, Arjuna shall come, guarded by the Pāñcālas.'"

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye maheṣvāso bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ āgamiṣyati dhunvāno gadāṃ daṇḍam ivāntakaḥ
english: "'In their midst, Bhīmasena the great archer, of mighty strength, shall come brandishing his mace like the staff of Yama.'"

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā pārthasya dhīmataḥ gadāvegaṃ ca bhīmasya nālaṃ soḍhuṃ narādhipāḥ
english: "'Then, having heard the twang of Arjuna's Gāṇḍīva and felt the impact of Bhīma's mace, no king shall be able to withstand it.'"

sanskrit: tatra me rocate nityaṃ pārthaiḥ sārdhaṃ na vigrahaḥ kurubhyo hi sadā manye pāṇḍavāñ śaktimattarān
english: "'In this matter, it has always seemed right to me that there be no conflict with the sons of Pṛthā; for I always consider the Pāṇḍavas more powerful than the Kurus.'"

sanskrit: tathā hi balavān rājā jarāsaṃdho mahādyutiḥ bāhupraharaṇenaiva bhīmena nihato yudhi
english: "'For indeed the powerful king Jarāsandha, of great splendour, was slain in battle by Bhīma with his bare arms alone.'"

sanskrit: tasya te śama evāstu pāṇḍavair bharatarṣabha ubhayoḥ pakṣayor yuktaṃ kriyatām aviśaṅkayā
english: "'Therefore let there be peace between you and the Pāṇḍavas, O bull of the Bharatas; let what is right for both sides be done without hesitation.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ gāvalgaṇe kṣattā dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ uktavān na gṛhītaṃ ca mayā putrahitepsayā
english: "Thus Vidura, son of Gavalgaṇa, spoke words encompassing both dharma and worldly good — and I did not accept them, being eager for the welfare of my son."
